text:
maria: noticed ~6 nodes in us-west1-preemptible-gpu are showing NotReady/NoSchedule, autoscaler is stuck scaling because pods can't be scheduled :thinking_face:
raj: looking now — kubelet on those nodes reports 'Failed to start device plugin: permission denied' and the nvidia-device-plugin pods are CrashLoopBackOff
sylvia: any recent kernel/image rollouts to that nodepool?
maria: we pushed a node image update last night to roll kernel from 5.10->5.15 for security patches, targeted the preemptible gpu pool only
raj: daemonset logs show this repeatedly:
```
I0321 12:03:04.123456 1 deviceplugin.go:87] error: failed to open /dev/nvidiactl: permission denied
E0321 12:03:04.123460 1 plugin.go:201] device plugin initialization failed: unable to load nvidia kernel module
```
raj: looks like kernel ABI mismatch with our nvidia driver package on the image — nodes boot but /dev nodes not created so device plugin exits
maria: cluster-autoscaler is refusing to drain because pods are non-evictable (hostNetwork kube-system addons + some operator DaemonSets) — so nodes stay tainted NoSchedule and CA can't replace capacity
oncall: infra-bot alert: `GPU pool us-west1-preemptible: 6 nodes NotReady — device-plugin crashloop` (pager attached)
sylvia: temp mitigation: mark nodepool as unschedulable for new workloads and spin up a dedicated non-preemptible gpu pool with working image, then cordon + drain failing nodes one-by-one after fixing evictions
raj: trying a quick patch: updating nvidia-device-plugin DS to use init container that checks /dev and retries, plus tolerate NotReady for a bit. command I ran: `kubectl patch daemonset nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"initContainers":[{"name":"wait-dev","image":"busybox","command":["sh","-c","for i in $(seq 1 30); do [ -e /dev/nvidiactl ] && exit 0 || sleep 2; done; exit 1"]}]}}}}'`
maria: that makes plugin wait but doesn't fix missing kernel module. Can we revert node image or reinstall driver on the nodes?
sylvia: for preemptibles we don't traditionally SSH them. Option A: revert the image rollout via cloud-machinepool rolling update. Option B: push a gke-addon style driver update DaemonSet that installs matching driver into host (hacky). Prefer revert image for safety
oncall: oncall: if we revert, autoscaler will try to scale down and might evict GPUs during eviction grace; we'll need to set `--max-empty-bulk-delete` lower and watch GPU churn
raj: quick log from kubelet on one node:
```
Feb 21 11:59:02 kubelet[1234]: mount: /dev/nvidia0: no such file or directory
Feb 21 11:59:03 device-plugin[1]: cannot register: failed to list devices
```
maria: I'm going to start a rollback of the nodepool image for the preemptible pool, rolling 2 nodes at a time. Also opening a change to create a short-lived non-preemptible pool to absorb traffic
sylvia: also file a follow-up to add a gating step to image rollouts for GPU nodepools: smoke test that nvidia modules load before marking rollout complete
oncall: oncall: coordinating with autoscaler — temporarily set CA `--scale-down-unneeded-time` to 10m so it gives nodes time to recover after rollback; lowering risk of flapping
raj: note for postmortem: device-plugin should surface explicit kernel-driver mismatch message; current error is generic permission/open error. We'll add more checks in plugin init to detect module presence and kernel version mismatch
maria: rollback in progress. will post when first node is Ready and device-plugin stays Running
(20m later)
maria: update: first 2 nodes rolled back, kubelet now shows /dev/nvidia* and device-plugin -> Running. Autoscaler started rebalancing and some pending pods scheduled :party_parrot:
raj: keeping an eye on remaining nodes. We'll still follow up with a P0 to add pre-rollback smoke tests and an alert that specifically mentions "nvidia module missing" to reduce MTTR
sylvia: noted. I'll open the ticket to add gating and a driver-version compatibility check into image pipelines
oncall: infra-bot: incident resolved for us-west1-preemptible-gpu (nodes recovered).
